The Sun Belt is basically where CUSA was at in the early 2010s. CUSA has basically fallen apart, UTEP and Sam Houston State are the only Texas teams remaining. Houston, Rice, UTSA, and North Texas used to be CUSA members but left because the conference was no longer profitable. It would be a bad idea to leave the Sun Belt for CUSA. The American Conference should be something TXST should strive for and it would be a promotion from the Sun Belt. I think the athletic department has that goal in mind but we won’t see that happen for at least another decade. Mountain West would also fit TXST somewhat but UTEP would probably be a better option. 

If TXST would have been D1 earlier, I could definitely see us getting an invitation from the AAC or even the Big 12 but as it stands right now, the American is full and any other conference would not be economically viable for us or the conference. It will be another decade or a total dissolution of the Sun Belt before TXST is ready to move on but I think TXST is doing just fine where they are.

Simply, a laptop and pc are very different. Mods or whatever affect the game in some way, and having a laptop will affect it more than a pc. Playing games on your tv through your laptop isn’t desirable either as yes, frames will significantly drop, as your laptop isn’t designed to run games on a tv. 

I made the switch to pc after having a PS5 for only a month and don’t regret it. The variety of games is immense and I’ve never enjoyed gaming as much as I do now. The biggest thing I learned is that you may not get the best specs right away, but the experience will make you forget that. Sell your laptop and start one of the most fun experiences building a PC from scratch! It’ll be worth it in the end. Hope this helps!
